title: code.query authoring is blind: no tree-sitter node-kind introspection
wanted_capability: Query-authoring support for cells, two halves. (1) Binding half: code.nodeKinds(file|language) enumerating valid tree-sitter node type names (and ideally field names). (2) Doc half — operator direction 2026-06-12: as the query surface expands, do NOT keep growing inline declaration prose; create an sm-tree-sitter system memory holding per-language grammar guidance + example queries, and signpost it from the tool docs/declarations ("use bbox_knowledge to read sm-tree-sitter before authoring code queries"). Caveat for the signpost: standalone harness probes have no bbox MCP surface — daemon dispatches can follow it from cells via tools.mcp__blackbox__bbox_knowledge, standalone agents need the binding half or inline minimum. Probe-2 evidence sharpened the failure mode: a VALID query returning empty captures collapsed the agent's confidence in the whole namespace (now mitigated by an empty-vs-invalid line in the declarations, but the deep fix is grammar knowledge on demand).
missing_primitive: code.nodeKinds(language) binding + example queries in declarations
fallback_used: Abandoned semantic queries after 2 failed cells; fell back to a structural (function_item (visibility_modifier)) query plus code.read + JS string matching.
evidence: prompts/RETRO_ISOLATE_REFACTOR.md retro findings: query-authoring x2, errors
notes: Inline mitigations landed (commits 27b8236, and the probe-3 round): two example queries, empty-vs-invalid semantics, node-kind provenance note. These are holding the line but are exactly the inline growth the operator wants capped — next expansion goes to sm-tree-sitter + signpost instead.
